messages:
sophia_pm: Heads-up — customer ACME hit a bunch of mismatched errors across chat + embeddings when hitting spikes. We need a short decision on canonical status codes and the SDK surface before next week's beta cut. Specifically: rate limits, input validation, model-unavailable/capacity, and function-calling/schema validation.
kevin_eng: Good call. Can we list what callers care about? my brain: retryable vs non-retryable, machine-readable code, human message, Retry-After header when applicable.
anya_devex: +1. SDKs need stable mapping: e.g. SDK should expose typed exceptions (RateLimitError, ValidationError, ModelUnavailableError) and surface retry_after where present. Docs + examples too.
marcos_support: From support tickets: customers expect 429 with Retry-After for short bursts; when capacity gone for >30s they see 503 and assume permanent. We should make the distinction explicit.
mike_p: Proposed minimal HTTP mapping: 429=rate_limit (transient, Retry-After), 413=payload_too_large (input tokens too big), 422=invalid_schema/structured-output-failure, 409=model_version_conflict (pinned version mismatch), 503=model_unavailable (transient capacity/op state). Thoughts?
kevin_eng: Mostly OK. One nuance: for embeddings we often return validation errors for empty or non-string inputs — I'd prefer 400 for generic validation (bad request) and 422 for semantic validation where payload is syntactically OK but semantically invalid (e.g., structured output failed to match schema).
sophia_pm: So use 400 for simple validation + parameter errors, 422 for structured/format validation. Keep 429/503 semantics as mike suggested. Agree?
anya_devex: For function/tool calling: missing tool -> 404? or 422? I think 404 makes sense if a referenced tool id doesn't exist. Validation of args -> 422. Also recommend SDK translate 503->ModelUnavailableError(retryable=true) vs 500->InternalError(retryable=false).
marcos_support: Customer reported billing/quota blocks returning 403 which confused them. Can we standardize quota exceeded -> 402 or 403? 402 (Payment Required) is weird. I'd vote for 403 with code=quota_exceeded and a clear user_facing_message + upgrade link.
mike_p: Agree to keep 403 for quota/permission. Reserve 402 for future billing flows if we expose card-on-file failures.
kevin_eng: Quick sample canonical error payload we should standardize (proto for docs):
```json
{
  "error": {
    "status": 429,
    "code": "rate_limit",
    "message": "Request rate too high; retry in Xs",
    "retry_after": 12,
    "user_facing": "Too many requests. Try again in 12s.",
    "docs_url": "https://docs.redwood.ai/errors#rate_limit"
  }
}
```
anya_devex: That looks good. SDK should expose error.code and error.retry_after and attach HTTP headers too. Also include a short machine-readable category: retryable / client_error / server_error.
sophia_pm: Launch gating checklist I propose: 1) Spec PR merged with canonical codes + examples; 2) SDK mapping for JS/Python; 3) Console display for rate-limits/quota with clear CTA; 4) E2E tests that simulate bursts + model-fallbacks; 5) Support KB + canned responses. Anyone object?
marcos_support: Sounds good. Add: sample customer-facing phrasing for each code (we'll reuse in KB).
mike_p: Dev question: model fallback behavior — when we fallback to smaller model due to capacity, what status do we return? my suggestion: success but add header X-Model-Fallback + structured field warnings; only return 503 if no fallback available.
kevin_eng: Agreed. Prefer silent fallback with a warning unless policy forbids it; never return 503 if a compatible fallback served the request. 503 reserved for when no compatible variant is available.
anya_devex: For SDKs, expose a Warning object when fallback occurred so apps can log/regress. e.g., warnings: [{"code":"model_fallback","from":"gpt-x-large","to":"gpt-x-small"}]
sophia_pm: Outstanding action items: Kevin to draft spec PR with table of codes + canonical payloads; Anya to write SDK mapping notes; Marcos to draft KB blurbs. Target: PR by Wed EOD. Kevin, you good to own the PR? :thumbsup:
kevin_eng: I can do it. Will drop a draft and ping for review by Tuesday.
marcos_support: I'll prepare the KB stubs and paste into the PR.
anya_devex: Will add SDK examples and tests once spec lands.
ops-bot: Reminder: automerge rules require 1 reviewer from eng + 1 from product for spec PRs.
sophia_pm: Great, thanks team. We'll reconvene if anything unexpected pops up.
